boundary: Grade actual communicated scoped meaning and original citations. No word-overlap score; all essential needs remain frozen including difficult causal/scope limitations.

questions.question: Compare SAME samples 2 and 3 for material, air flow, weight-loss rate and aging duration. Keep the recorded units and each sample association. Do these rows alone justify attributing a rate difference to aging?
essential_needs: Both source samples are Teflon
Both air flows are 5 cm/s
Sample 2 weight-loss rate 1 mg/min and aging duration 1 minute
Sample 3 weight-loss rate 2 mg/min and aging duration 20 minutes
No new causal explanation inferred from these records alone

questions.question: What fuel and calibration information is recorded in the SLICE entries dated 9 February 2012 and 13 February 2012? Describe the scope of those source entries.
essential_needs: 9 February entry 100% CH4
13 February entry 40% CH4 balance N2
13 February includes two pyrometry calibration tests and two fan calibrations
Entries are source sessions; no invented individual-run enumeration

questions.question: For BASS-II B5, quote the material description as written, the initial and final CO and CO2 entries, and the radiometer gain setting.
essential_needs: Material cell literal 200 micron  2 cm wide, without inserting a material identity
Initial CO 0 ppm and final CO 12 ppm
Initial and final CO2 both 0.43 percent by volume
Radiometer gain 50, as a setting

questions.question: For that same B5 record, what are the calibrated initial and final oxygen concentrations? Keep oxygen separate from the CO and CO2 entries.
essential_needs: BASS-II B5 scope retained from preceding turn
Calibrated initial oxygen 22.2 percent by volume
Calibrated final oxygen 21.9 percent by volume
Oxygen values are not substituted for CO or CO2

questions.question: For pure isooctane, what gas-mixture choices, oxygen fractions and flow-velocity range does FLEX-2 list? Explain what the configuration summary establishes about physical run identities.
essential_needs: Pure isooctane configuration scope
Ambient choices O2/N2 or O2/He
Oxygen mole fractions 0.17, 0.21, 0.25 and 0.3
Flow velocity 0.1 to 5 cm/s
No invented identified physical runs or Cartesian condition combinations

questions.question: In NASA-STD-6001B with Change 3, what information does Test 2 provide, how is heat-release rate determined, and is a pass/fail criterion specified for that test?
essential_needs: Test 2 is Heat and Visible Smoke Release Rates and provides supplemental flammability information
Information includes effective heat of combustion, time to ignition, heat-release rate, smoke obscuration and total heat released
Heat-release rate determined from oxygen-consumption measurement
No pass/fail criterion associated with Test 2; results may contribute to fire-risk assessment

questions.question: What does the ACME ISS overview report about the fuel and flame configuration associated with the CFI-G cool-flame images, the camera filtering, and the size comparison with hot flames?
essential_needs: Cool flames discovered during normal-flame CFI-G tests with n-butane
Intensified camera filtered for formaldehyde emissions
Reported cool flames smaller than corresponding hot flames
Report-specific findings not transferred to every fuel or configuration

questions.question: Compare the inverse-flame configuration described for Flame Design with the way BRE emulates condensed-phase burning in the ACME ISS overview. Explain what each method investigates.
essential_needs: Flame Design studies normal and inverse ethylene/oxygen flame configurations and soot inception/flow direction
In an inverse flame oxidizer exits the burner into an atmosphere of gaseous fuel
BRE uses a flat porous burner with gaseous fuel to emulate burning of solids and liquids
BRE measures thermal feedback and matches combustion/gasification heats, surface temperature and smoke point
Emulation and methods are not described as direct observations of actual solid samples
